title: Vedanta seeks premium over imported LNG prices for Rajasthan gas sale
description:
Vedanta Oil and Gas Ltd is seeking a premium over imported LNG prices for 1.80 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) of natural gas from its Rajasthan block, putting the volume up for sale through an electronic auction.
The three-month supply contract, running from January 1 to April 1, 2027, will be auctioned on December 14, according to a request for proposal dated November 20 and a draft gas sales agreement.
Bidders have been asked to quote a premium they are willing to pay over the monthly average of Platts West India spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices, with the highest bids receiving priority in the allocation of available volumes.
The starting premium is zero, with bids required to increase in increments of at least USD 0.05 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), according to the tender document.
The offered volume is equivalent to approximately 75,600 MMBtu per day, or about 6.8 million MMBtu over the 90-day contract period.
